props.title: Children of God
props.initialSlug: In the name of the father.

sections.content: **Children of God (1994)** (1994) represents a pivotal documentary examining religious cults and their impact on children, following in the haunting footsteps of films like **Jonestown: The Life and Death of Peoples Temple** (2006). The film's raw exploration of the Children of God cult became a blueprint for later cult documentaries like **Holy Hell** (2016) and **Prophet's Prey** (2015), establishing conventions for handling sensitive interview footage and archival materials while protecting vulnerable subjects.

sections.content: The documentary tradition of investigating religious movements gained significant momentum in the 1990s, with **Paradise Lost: The Child Murders at Robin Hood Hills** (1996) examining religious paranoia's devastating community effects. **Children of God** (1994) shares this era's unflinching approach to controversial subject matter, while maintaining crucial ethical boundaries when documenting minors in dangerous situations. SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Cult Documentation

Contemporary filmmakers continue building on techniques pioneered in **Children of God** (1994). **The Source Family** (2012) borrowed its intimate interview style, while **The Vow** (2020) expanded the format into a series-length investigation. These films demonstrate how documentary approaches to controversial religious movements evolved from straightforward exposé to nuanced character studies.
